newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-STANGASSINGER LEADS NIGHT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-STANGASSINGER LEADS NIGHT SLALOM.

text.p: Austria's Thomas Stangassinger delighted home fans on Thursday by taking the lead after the first run of the World Cup season's first men's night slalom.b The reigning Olympic champion clocked 46.72 seconds on the perfectly prepared Planai piste, flagged with 57 gates.
He was trailed by last year's overall slalom World Cup winner Sebastien Amiez of France (46.87) and Italian Olympic and world champion Alberto Tomba (46.94).
For Tomba -- and most other competitors -- the race was ideal preparation for the February 16 world championship slalom in Sestriere, which will also be decided under lights.
Austria's Thomas Sykora, dominant figure in men's slalom this winter, disappointed with a ninth best 47.51.
Sykora was still suffering from hip pains received during a heavy fall in a warm-up for last Sunday's slalom in Kitzbuehel.
Missing in Schladming was 1996 world championship slalom silver medallist Mario Reiter of Austria. He has a slight bout of influenza and decided to save himself for Sestriere.
